newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Japan gives Sri Lanka 36 bln yen in soft loans.
newsitem.headline: Japan gives Sri Lanka 36 bln yen in soft loans.

text.p: Sri Lanka said it had signed an agreement with Japan on Friday under which Tokyo would extend six soft loans amounting to nearly 36 billion yen ($314 million).
The loans would be for improving power transmission, roads, telecommunications, water supply, irrigation systems and to develop small scale industries, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
It said the loans were repayable over 30 years and include a 10-year grace period.
Japan is one of the Indian Ocean island's biggest aid donors.
The Finance Ministry also said Norway had granted 125 million rupees ($2.14 million) for a five-year programme on national integration to support government efforts to establish communal harmony.
"The programme would support education and training to promote the vision of Sri Lanka as a multi-ethnic society," the statement said.

It would also support research and advise on issues relating to national integration, and promotional and protection activities to ensure non-discrimination and equality of the treatment for Sri Lankan citizens.
The country has been wracked by fighting between government forces and Tamil Tiger rebels since 1983. The rebels seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka.

Earlier this week, the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) gave Sri Lanka $3 million to develop financial markets and small businesses, expand markets for agro-enterprises and meet technology needs of the private sector.
